Tourists and visitors looked askance at the Penwhinnock folk, and avoided their houses as if they had contained the plague, so that few strangers ever came among them or conversed with them.

arxiv-1403-7494.title: Some characterizations of slant and spherical helices due to sabban frame
arxiv-1403-7494.creator: B. Altunkaya, L. Kula
arxiv-1403-7494.description: Abstract In this paper, we are investigating that under which conditions of the geodesic curvature of unit speed curve γ \gamma that lies on the unit sphere, the curve c c which is obtained by using γ \gamma , is a spherical helix or slant helix. Key Words: Helices, Spherical Helices, Slant Helices, Sabban Frame.

arxiv-2110-01238.title: Overdamped limit at stationarity for non-equilibrium Langevin diffusions
arxiv-2110-01238.creator: Pierre Monmarché, Mouad Ramil
arxiv-2110-01238.description: Abstract In this note, we establish that the stationary distribution of a possibly non-equilibrium Langevin diffusion converges, as the damping parameter goes to infinity (or equivalently in the Smoluchowski-Kramers vanishing mass limit), toward a tensor product of the stationary distribution of the corresponding overdamped process and of a Gaussian distribution.

arxiv-2203-00955.title: GRASP EARTH: Intuitive Software for Discovering Changes on the Planet
arxiv-2203-00955.creator: Waku Hatakeyama, Shirou Kawakita, Ryohei Izawa, Masanari Kimura
arxiv-2203-00955.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Waku Hatakeyama, Shirou Kawakita, Ryohei Izawa, Masanari Kimura. Detecting changes on the Earth, such as urban development, deforestation, or natural disaster, is one of the research fields that is attracting a great deal of attention. One promising tool to solve these problems is satellite imagery. However, satellite images require huge amount of storage, therefore users are required to set Area of Interests first, which was not suitable for detecting potential areas for disaster or development.

arxiv-2204-02064.title: PERKS: a Locality-Optimized Execution Model for Iterative Memory-bound GPU Applications Conference: 2023 International Conference on Supercomputing; June 21–23, 2023; Orlando, FL, USA 2023 International Conference on Supercomputing (ICS ’23), June 21–23, 2023, Orlando, FL, USA Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1
arxiv-2204-02064.creator: Lingqi Zhang, Mohamed Wahib, Peng Chen, Jintao Meng, Xiao Wang, Toshio Endo, Satoshi Matsuoka
arxiv-2204-02064.description: Abstract . Iterative memory-bound solvers commonly occur in HPC codes. Typical GPU implementations have a loop on the host side that invokes the GPU kernel as much as time/algorithm steps there are. The termination of each kernel implicitly acts the barrier required after advancing the solution every time step.

arxiv-2211-04121.title: Ferroelectric higher-order topological insulator in two dimensions
arxiv-2211-04121.creator: Ning Mao, Runhan Li, Xiaorong Zou, Ying Dai, Baibiao Huang, Chengwang Niu
arxiv-2211-04121.description: Abstract The interplay between ferroelectricity and band topology can give rise to a wide range of both fundamental and applied research. Here, we map out the emergence of nontrivial corner states in two-dimensional ferroelectrics, and remarkably demonstrate that ferroelectricity and corner states are coupled together by crystallographic symmetry to realize the electric control of higher-order topology.

arxiv-2302-09761.title: An indirect method for solving combinatorial problems
arxiv-2302-09761.creator: M. Shevtsova, A. Kanel-Belov, M. Golafshan
arxiv-2302-09761.description: Abstract . This article introduces a pedagogical method for solving combinatorial problems that frequently involve structures that are unfamiliar or less familiar. Indeed, an indirect method has been proposed in order to evade any possible questions that might obstruct our path to the correct answer and final solution. With this method, the desired configuration can be formulated.

arxiv-2309-12704.title: Searching for Smurfs: Testing if Money Launderers Know Alert Thresholds
arxiv-2309-12704.creator: Rasmus Ingemann Tuffveson Jensen, Joras Ferwerda, Christian Remi Wewer
arxiv-2309-12704.description: Abstract To combat money laundering, banks raise and review alerts on transactions that exceed confidential thresholds. This paper presents a data-driven approach to detect smurfing, i.e., money launderers seeking to evade detection by breaking up large transactions into amounts under the secret thresholds.

arxiv-2312-13026.title: FusDom: Combining In-Domain and Out-of-Domain Knowledge for Continuous Self-Supervised Learning
arxiv-2312-13026.creator: Ashish Seth, Sreyan Ghosh, S. Umesh, Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2312-13026.description: Abstract Continued pre-training (CP) offers multiple advantages, like target domain adaptation and the potential to exploit the continuous stream of unlabeled data available online. However, continued pre-training on out-of-domain distributions often leads to catastrophic forgetting of previously acquired knowledge, leading to sub-optimal ASR performance. This paper presents FusDom, a simple and novel methodology for SSL-based continued pre-training.

arxiv-2410-10871.title: Applying Refusal-Vector Ablation to Llama 3.1 70B Agents Thanks: https://www.apartresearch.com/
arxiv-2410-10871.creator: Simon Lermen, Mateusz Dziemian, Govind Pimpale
arxiv-2410-10871.description: Abstract Recently, language models like Llama 3.1 Instruct have become increasingly capable of agentic behavior, enabling them to perform tasks requiring short-term planning and tool use. In this study, we apply refusal-vector ablation to Llama 3.1 70B and implement a simple agent scaffolding to create an unrestricted agent.

arxiv-2412-05619.title: Do We Need to Design Specific Diffusion Models for Different Tasks? Try ONE-PIC
arxiv-2412-05619.creator: Ming Tao, Bing-Kun Bao, Yaowei Wang, Changsheng Xu
arxiv-2412-05619.description: Abstract Large pretrained diffusion models have demonstrated impressive generation capabilities and have been adapted to various downstream tasks. However, unlike Large Language Models (LLMs) that can learn multiple tasks in a single model based on instructed data, diffusion models always require additional branches, task-specific training strategies, and losses for effective adaptation to different downstream tasks.

arxiv-2503-13664.title: Dynamics of defects and interfaces for interacting quantum hard disks
arxiv-2503-13664.creator: Fabian Ballar Trigueros, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, Markus Heyl
arxiv-2503-13664.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fabian Ballar Trigueros, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, Markus Heyl. Defects and interfaces are essential to understand the properties of matter. However, studying their dynamics in the quantum regime remains a challenge in particular concerning the regime of two spatial dimensions. Recently, it has been shown that a quantum counterpart of the hard-disk problem on a lattice yields defects and interfaces, which are stable just due to quantum effects while they delocalize and dissolve in an analogous classical stochastic process.

arxiv-2505-21762.title: Convergence of linear solutions through convergence of periodic initial data
arxiv-2505-21762.creator: Harrison Gaebler, Wesley R. Perkins
arxiv-2505-21762.description: Abstract When studying the stability of T T -periodic solutions to partial differential equations, it is common to encounter subharmonic perturbations, i.e. perturbations which have a period that is an integer multiple (say n n ) of the background wave, and localized perturbations, i.e. perturbations that are integrable on the line.

pmc-10597236.creator: S Gözüm, G Yurcu, A Ilgaz, D H Aybar
pmc-10597236.description: BackgroundTo provide the optimum level of health and tourism goals of Turkey, it is important that the supply of well-trained health and tourism professionals meets the demand. Our study aimed to evaluate the sequential mediating role of self-efficacy and financial anxiety levels in the impact of health and tourism students’ life satisfaction on their migration attitudes.

pmc-11335811.title: Comparisons of clinical scoring systems among suspected pulmonary embolism patients presenting to emergency department
pmc-11335811.creator: Luojia Tang, Yundi Hu, Min Min, Jianyong Gu, Dong Pan, Xiaolei Lin, Chaoyang Tong
pmc-11335811.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionPulmonary embolism (PE) is among the most severe cardiovascular disorders worldwide. Timely and appropriate diagnosis of PE remains an important step in reducing PE related mortality and morbidity.MethodsIn this retrospective single‐center cohort study, we comprehensively compared the screening performances of several clinical scoring systems (Wells score [WS], Revised Geneva score [RGS], WS + d‐Dimer [D‐D], RGS + D‐D, WS + PE rule‐out criteria [PERC] and RGS + PERC) among PE suspected patients.

pmc-11532904.title: Hematopoietic cells emerging from hemogenic endothelium exhibit lineage-specific oxidative stress responses
pmc-11532904.creator: Harmke Biezeman, Martina Nubiè, Leal Oburoglu
pmc-11532904.description: During human embryogenesis, distinct waves of hematopoiesis give rise to various blood cell types, originating from hemogenic endothelial (HE) cells. As HE cells reside in hypoxic conditions in the embryo, we investigated the role of hypoxia in human endothelial to hematopoietic transition and subsequent hematopoiesis.

pmc-11546271.creator: Siddig I. Abdelwahab, Manal M.E. Taha, Sivakumar S. Sivagurunathan Moni, Mahdi M. Alnajai, Ahmed A. Jerah, Abdullah Farasani, Saleh M. Abdullah, Ieman A. Aljahdali, Omar Oraibi, Bassem Oraibi, Hassan A. Alfaifi, Amal H. Alzahrani, Yasir O.H. Babiker, Adel S. Al-Zubairi
pmc-11546271.description: BackgroundThis study examined the effects of khat extract on the proinflammatory cytokines, liver, and kidneys of rats. Unlike previous research that focused on broad immune markers and general effects, this study investigated specific proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, and TNF-α) and considered gender differences in the immune response.

pmc-11617720.creator: Sakura Sato, Noriyuki Yanagida, Ken-ichi Nagakura, Kyohei Takahashi, Magnus P Borres, Motohiro Ebisawa

We aimed to quantitatively evaluate the clinical importance of sensitization to Ara h 6 in managing peanut allergy in Japanese children.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed the data of children with or without symptoms induced by an oral food challenge or home dosing of up to 3 g of peanuts.

pmc-12452933.creator: Zhimin Jiang, Wenliang Pan, Yu Chen, Dongliang Zhou, Shuning Ren, Qi Tong, Litao Liu, Honglei Sun, Yipeng Sun, Yuhai Bi, Dayan Wang, Lu Lu, Juan Pu, Kin-Chow Chang, Jinhua Liu

Additionally, the global population is aging at an unprecedented rate in human history, posing major issues for healthcare and the economy. Thus, there is an urgent need to understand the pathogenesis of severe influenza affecting older patients.

pmc-12767600.title: Temporal distortion may mediate the association between problematic mobile gaming and delay discounting: An experimental study
pmc-12767600.creator: Da-I Huang, Ting-Hsi Chou, Chih-Chun Huang, Yun-Hsuan Chang, Chieh-Liang Huang, Mark D. Griffiths, Marc N. Potenza
pmc-12767600.description: BackgroundImpulsivity and delay discounting are considered core components of addiction and are increasingly associated with problematic mobile gaming. However, the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. Emerging evidence suggests that altered time perception may contribute to impulsive decision-making in addictive behaviors.

pmc-12828671.title: Outcomes of aortic and mitral valve replacement with Dafodil™ pericardial bioprosthesis over 5-years: Dafodil™-1 trial

S. Rajput, Rajan Sethuratnam, Naman Shastri,
pmc-12828671.description: ObjectivesThe durability and performance of bioprosthetic valves are pivotal in managing valvular heart disease (VHD). This 5-year follow-up study evaluated the long-term clinical safety, haemodynamic performance, and quality-of-life (QoL) outcomes of the Dafodil™ pericardial bioprosthesis in patients undergoing aortic or mitral valve replacement (AVR/MVR).

pmc-13072295.title: The Metabolic Calibration of Female Immune Plasticity: From X-Linked Vulnerability to Precision Metabotyping
pmc-13072295.creator: Zhengsha Huang, Jianwei Ren, Qipeng Shu, Yuntao Tang, Jia Zhang, Weizhe Yu, Chenxi Zhang, Yafang Pang, Lu Liu, Jiayue Han, Youfan Zhang, Weizhou Wang, Shangze Li
pmc-13072295.description: Simple SummaryBiological females generally exhibit more robust immune responses than males, which provides superior protection against infections but significantly increases the risk of autoimmune diseases such as lupus. This review explores why this disparity exists by introducing the Metabolic Calibration Hypothesis.

pmc-13098479.title: Synthesis of Conjugated Linear and Cyclic Polyynes by Selective Alkyne Metathesis
pmc-13098479.creator: Julien Escudero, Jonathan Long, Dylan Bouëtard, Jennifer Morvan, Mehdi Koohgard, Angelika Neitzel, Dirk Bockfeld, Shedrack Nwachukwu, Thierry Roisnel, Rik R Tykwinski, Matthias Tamm, Marc Mauduit, Yann Trolez
pmc-13098479.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The formation of polyynes with an odd number of conjugated triple bonds is synthetically demanding, particularly for complex architectures, since most established methods rely on irreversible C–C bond‐forming reactions and operate under kinetic control. To address this problem, we have developed the synthesis of triynes via molybdenum‐catalyzed alkyne metathesis of diynes, which allows thermodynamic control through reversible cleavage and formation of carbon–carbon triple bonds.

pmc-13236275.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Parental Guidance in Pediatric Orthopaedics: A Pilot Feasibility Study

pmc-13236275.description: Background:Parents of children with pediatric orthopaedic conditions frequently have questions after their clinic visit, and a reliable postconsultation resource to address these enquiries is lacking. Online resources are variable in quality, and general purpose artificial intelligence (AI) models have demonstrated safety limitations, including unprompted treatment recommendations and citation inaccuracies.

pmc-13586066.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Over Plasma Links Analytes to Cognitive Decline in Older Adults at Risk for Alzheimer's Disease
pmc-13586066.creator: Jagan A Pillai, Audrey Zhu, Chunxuan Ma, Ming Wang, Yifan Yang, Lynn M Bekris, Maria Khrestian, Frank P DiFilippo, Mikhail Nasrallah, Aaron Burberry, James B Leverenz, Yuan Hou, Feixiong Cheng, Stephen M Rao
pmc-13586066.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo identify inflammatory analytes in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma associated with cognitive decline in cognitively normal (CN) older adults at risk for Alzheimer's disease (AD).MethodsIn a longitudinal study of 118 CN older adults (65–80 years, 54% APOE ε4, 26% preclinical AD), 1331 CSF and 1501 plasma analytes were quantified at baseline and 2‐year follow‐up using SomaLogic, with key inflammatory findings validated on the Luminex platform. Linear models (Limma), adjusted for age, sex, APOEε4, and amyloid‐positive status, identified pathology‐associated analytes.

pmc-13632576.title: Combined Minimally Invasive Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion and Minimally Invasive Laminectomy
pmc-13632576.creator: Katherine Bunch, Simon Ammanuel, Bradley Schmidt
pmc-13632576.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) is a well-established intervention for patients with spondylolisthesis and instability with compression of neural structures. Minimally invasive (MIS) TLIF has been proposed as potentially superior to a standard midline approach. For patients with both bilateral lateral recess stenosis and central stenosis, combining MIS-TLIF with MIS laminectomy allows for bilateral decompression, which is not usually afforded by standard TLIF, in addition to arthrodesis.

pmc-13685453.title: Effects of starch structure on the absorption of encapsulated amino acids in laying hens fed low-protein diets
pmc-13685453.creator: Zhengkai Yue, Minghui Wang, Min Liu, Xiaojuan Wang, Jingpeng Zhao, Hongchao Jiao, Hai Lin
pmc-13685453.description: Low-protein (LP) diets supplemented with encapsulated crystalline amino acids (CAAs) have been proven to improve amino acid absorption kinetics and post-absorptive amino acid balance. This study investigated the effects of dietary starch structure, expressed as the amylose-to-amylopectin ratio (AAR), on encapsulated amino acid (EAA) utilization and laying performance in hens fed LP diets.
